FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Alphabet Flashcards A–Z

Twenty-six picture cards, one for every letter from A to Z. Big letters, little letters, familiar things to name — pick a card, say it together and stop whenever your preschooler has had enough.

These cards belong to Preschool · Age 3 on the Kiddo School learning path.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Three cards is a lovely day

    Pick a few, look at them slowly and stop while it is still fun. You do not need to finish the alphabet in one sitting — or even in one week.

  2. 02

    Start with your child’s own letter

    The first letter of your child’s name is the most interesting letter in the world to them. Begin there and watch how proudly they find it.

  3. 03

    Say the sound, not just the name

    The letter is named A, but it says a — like the very start of apple. Say both, casually, and let your child copy whichever one they like.

  4. 04

    Give today’s card a home

    Tape the card of the day to the fridge or a bedroom door at your child’s eye level. Passing it again and again is quietly powerful practice.

      Apple Flashcard — Letter A for Preschoolers

      A big red apple, the very first card in the alphabet. Apples are one of the few words your preschooler already owns — snack time has done half the teaching for you. That makes A the friendliest possible place to start.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      An apple a day, and now the A to go with it — breakfast-table phonics.

      Sound and move

      Stand like the letter A — legs wide, arms crossed high — then wobble without falling.

      What it teaches

      First-letter pride, the aaaa sound, and proof that letters live on snacks.

      Print it like this

      Print on cardstock and lean it against the toaster.

      Grown-up tip

      Say aaaa while you slice — one crisp bite seals the sound.

      Letter sound

      The letter is named A, but in apple you hear its sound: aaa, the very first sound out of your mouth. Vowels have more than one sound — this short a is the one to start with.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Apple lesson on the Learning Path.

      Ball Flashcard — Letter B for Preschoolers

      A bouncy picture for a bouncy letter. B is one of the first letters children notice on their own — it starts ball, bath, bubbles and half the fun of the day. This card gives all of that a friendly face.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      Bouncing begins with B, and this card hands the letter to the yard game.

      Sound and move

      Roll the ball to each other, shouting B every time it changes hands.

      What it teaches

      Letter B in both sizes, the quick b sound, and gentle turn-taking.

      Print it like this

      Two copies work — one for indoors, one for the sandpit.

      Grown-up tip

      Keep b snappy, one brisk tap of sound, not a long buzz.

      Letter sound

      B makes a quick lip-pop sound: buh, like the start of ball and bubble. Press your lips together, pop them open and there it is.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Ball lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cat Flashcard — Letter C for Preschoolers

      A soft cat face for the letter C. Cats are household celebrities for three-year-olds — real ones, neighbour’s ones and the one in every second picture book — so this word usually gets an excited point.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      Cats run this house already, so the letter C arrives with a live-in teacher.

      Sound and move

      Take turns being the cat, one c sound per lazy stretch.

      What it teaches

      That C often sounds like k, plus first C-word collecting.

      Print it like this

      Hang it in the hallway where the cat holds court.

      Grown-up tip

      Borrow the teddy as a stand-in when the real cat naps.

      Letter sound

      Here the letter c says kuh, just like k does. C is a letter of many talents: it can also borrow the s sound in words like circle — but cat keeps it simple.

      Elephant Flashcard — Letter E for Preschoolers

      Fish Flashcard — Letter F for Preschoolers

      The long airy f sound and a brand-new watery word.

      Xylophone Flashcard — Letter X for Preschoolers

      A rainbow xylophone for the letter X — the alphabet’s most mysterious letter. Xylophone is the classic X word precisely because x is so shy at the beginnings of words, and this card makes that honest.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      X finally gets a card worth the mystery — an instrument no kitchen owns.

      Sound and move

      March two fingers along the card, one ks per invisible note.

      What it teaches

      X mostly ends words, plus the honest truth about xylophone.

      Print it like this

      Prop it on the piano, if one happens to exist.

      Grown-up tip

      X prefers the end of words — collect socks, boxes and ducks.

      Letter sound

      Here is the honest part: x is mostly an end-of-word sound — it finishes box and fox with a ksss. Xylophone actually starts with a z sound! Say the letter name — ex — and enjoy the word together.

      Yo-yo Flashcard — Letter Y for Preschoolers

      A playful yo-yo for the letter Y. Y is a two-job letter — it works as a sound and sometimes as a vowel — but on this card it is pure toy box fun, going down and coming back up.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      Yo-yos make Y the toy letter — up, down, and named the whole time.

      Sound and move

      Bounce a sock ball off the palm, saying yuh on every catch.

      What it teaches

      Yuh up front, plus the joy of a word that moves.

      Print it like this

      Round the corners off — toys get thrown, cards survive longer.

      Grown-up tip

      Yuh glides straight into the word — no pause, no y-uh split.

      Letter sound

      In yo-yo, y makes its friendly starting sound: yuh, like the start of yes and yarn. Say yuh-yo-yo and bounce your hand on each yuh.

      Teach it, step by step

      FLASHCARD · ALPHABET A–Z · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Zebra Flashcard — Letter Z for Preschoolers

      A striped zebra finishing the alphabet in style. Z is the grand finale letter, and the zebra’s bold stripes give little eyes something to trace with a finger — from the letter to the animal and back.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this letter card does

      Zebras close the alphabet in stripes and Z finishes what A started.

      Sound and move

      Zip up the duvet slowly, dragging one long zzz the whole way.

      What it teaches

      That zzz is s wearing a voice, plus finishing all twenty-six.

      Print it like this

      Last of the set — let your child notice the alphabet is complete.

      Grown-up tip

      Zzz belongs at bedtime — one each night, then sleep takes over.

      Letter sound

      Z is a buzzing bee sound: zzz, made exactly like s but with your voice switched on. Hold your throat — zzz — it purrs.

      Teach it, step by step
